newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open flat to 0.2 firmer.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open flat to 0.2 firmer.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open unchanged to 0.2 cent firmer Thursday, based on market orders at 1018 EDT, traders said.

USDA put new sales at 95,800 480-lb bales for the current crop, for the week ended April 10. Total commitments rose to 6.235 million bales. USDA has estimated that exports will reach 7.0 million bales in the current season.
Exports for the week were 180,200 bales, 28 percent below the previous week's marketing year high and 11 percent below the four-week average, USDA said.

Wednesday, NYCE cotton futures closed down sharply after hitting new contract lows in the front three months. Spot May finished 0.88 cent lower at 70.88 cents a lb after trading from 71.76 to 75.50 cents, a contract low. July went out down 0.86 at 72.54 after hitting a contract low of 72.20 cents.
((-- S Rostler, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1640))
